question: to the Commission Estrella Galán (The Left), Rima Hassan (The Left), Ilaria Salis (The Left), Oihane Agirregoitia Martínez (Renew), Kostas Papadakis (NI), Lefteris Nikolaou-Alavanos (NI), Marc Botenga (The Left), Manon Aubry (The Left), Giorgos Georgiou (The Left), Hana Jalloul Muro (S&D), Martin Günther (The Left), Vladimir Prebilič (Verts/ALE), Leila Chaibi (The Left), Ana Miranda Paz (Verts/ALE), Damien Carême (The Left), Estelle Ceulemans (S&D), Rudi Kennes (The Left), Pernando Barrena Arza (The Left), Vicent Marzà Ibáñez (Verts/ALE), Jaume Asens Llodrà (Verts/ALE), Benedetta Scuderi (Verts/ALE) Subject:

On 29 January 2026, the Trump administration signed a new executive order reinforcing the economic, commercial and financial blockade imposed by the United States against Cuba, including measures aimed at restricting the supply of oil and other energy resources to the island. These actions intensify an extraterritorial sanctions policy that has been repeatedly condemned by the international community, including by the UN General Assembly, because of its serious economic and humanitarian effects on the Cuban population. The restriction of access to essential energy resources is affecting the functioning of hospitals, transport systems, food production and other basic services. 1.
What measures does the Commission intend to implement to mitigate the humanitarian impact of this executive order in relation to Cuba’s access to essential fuels and energy?
Does the Commission consider that measures to prevent the supply of oil to a country are compatible with international law and the humanitarian principles that the EU claims to uphold?
What concrete action does the Commission intend to take to counter the extraterritorial application of these measures and to protect European economic operators in Cuba?
Supporters1
This question is supported by Members other than the authors: Danilo Della Valle (The Left), Maria Zacharia (NI).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.7.2026) Since 1994, the Commission has been actively engaged in addressing the most pressing needs of the Cuban population. In 2024-2025, it released close to EUR 10 million to provide lifesaving health services country-wide, and emergency relief to hurricane-stricken communities. As an immediate response to the steadfast deterioration of the humanitarian crisis in 2026, the Commission has allocated additional EUR 6 million for humanitarian aid actions, including the provision of logistic support to humanitarian agencies to mitigate the impact of the energy crisis on food and drinking water distribution and health services1. The implementation is closely monitored to ensure the assistance reaches the neediest, timely and effectively. The Commission stands ready to increase its support in this crisis and operates in strict compliance with the humanitarian principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality and independence. The EU aid is channelled exclusively through vetted, specialised humanitarian partners, including UN agencies and international non-governmental organisations. The Commission and the European External Action Service are closely monitoring the impact of the announced measures on EU economic operators in Cuba. The Commission will continue to underline the important contribution that EU economic operators can make to Cuba’s economic development, irrespective of the scenario that emerges in coming months. In parallel, the Commission will continue to emphasise the need to safeguard the rights of EU economic operators’ rights and the integrity of bilateral commercial interests.
